`TestNodeCanBeDeleted`, `TestSnapshotCanBeMade`, `TestNodesCanBeRestarted`,
  `TestLinearizableReadCanBeMade`, `TestNodeHostAddNode`,
  `TestNodeHostAddObserverRemoveNode`) pass 10/10 repetitions.
- Statement coverage: `internal/raft` 91.2%, root package 88.7%.
- `internal/transport`: the non-TLS tests (chunk assembly, chunk writer,
  registry, circuit breaker, initial message, in-memory send limits) pass in
  the isolated namespace. The TLS variants cannot run: the captured tree has
  `internal/transport/tests/localhost.crt` and `test-root-ca.crt` but no
  `localhost.key`, so `TestMessageCanBeSent` and the other mutual-TLS variants
  abort with `open tests/localhost.key: no such file or directory`. This is a
  packaging limitation, not an implementation failure; the TLS handshake path
  of `internal/transport/tcp.go` is therefore unaudited by execution.
  Because the TLS-first loops panic, the rest of the transport suite (snapshot
  sending/streaming, connection failure handling, circuit breakers) never
  ran in the captured tree. In a diagnostic copy (`audit/diag-transport/`)
  the TLS setup was first disabled to run every test on the non-TLS path
  (whole package passes, 13 s), then a fresh CA/server certificate pair was
  generated into the copy's `tests/` directory to run the mutual-TLS variants
  too (whole package passes, 14 s). The captured source was not modified.

The upstream test suite therefore does not exercise the defects below.

## Summary

| ID | Region | Defect | Evidence |
|----|--------|--------|----------|
| F1 | `nodehost.go` `(*nodeUser).ReadIndex` | Enqueues a ReadIndex request without waking the execution engine; the request is only dispatched by the next tick. Up to one RTT added latency; a one-RTT timeout deterministically returns `RequestTimeout` on a healthy cluster, while `NodeHost.ReadIndex` with the same timeout completes. | Executed (5/5 failures), latency measurement, causality check in `audit/diag`. |
| F2 | `internal/raft/raft.go` `handleCandidateReadIndex` | The dropped ReadIndex is recorded twice, so `pb.Update.DroppedReadIndexes` contains the same `SystemCtx` twice for one request. Currently idempotent downstream; the raft update is wrong. | Executed at raft level and through exported `Peer.GetUpdate`. |
| F3 | `raftpb/raft.go` `(*Update).HasUpdate` | Ignores `DroppedReadIndexes`: `Peer.HasUpdate` reports an update for a node whose only pending work is a dropped read index, while `Update.HasUpdate()` returns false for the very same update. No production caller of `Update.HasUpdate` exists in this tree. | Executed (`TestAuditUpdateHasUpdateWithDroppedReadIndexes`). |

## Finding 3 (executed, minor): `pb.Update.HasUpdate` ignores dropped read indexes

`raftpb.Update.HasUpdate` (`raftpb/raft.go:112`) checks state, snapshot,
entries to save, committed entries, messages, ready-to-reads and dropped
entries, but not `DroppedReadIndexes`. A node whose only pending work is a
dropped read index therefore reports `Peer.HasUpdate() == true` (peer.go does
check the field) while the `pb.Update` produced for that node reports
`HasUpdate() == false`. No production code in this tree calls
`Update.HasUpdate`, so the impact is limited to API consumers, but the two
layers disagree about the same state.

item.text:
This pass added a third (minor) finding and pinned down Finding 1's exact boundary.

**Finding 3 (new, executed): `pb.Update.HasUpdate` ignores dropped read indexes**

`raftpb.Update.HasUpdate` ([raftpb/raft.go](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_20-19-30-dragonboat_raft-baseline/work/raftpb/raft.go:112)) checks state, snapshot, entries-to-save, committed entries, messages, ready-to-reads and dropped entries — but not `DroppedReadIndexes`. A node whose only pending work is a dropped read index therefore reports `Peer.HasUpdate() == true` (peer.go checks the field) while the `pb.Update` produced for that node reports `HasUpdate() == false`. The test asserts the `Peer` side first, then the `Update` side, so the contradiction is between the two API layers:

```
zz_audit_repro_test.go:169: pb.Update.HasUpdate() reported false for an
    update carrying 2 dropped read index(es)
--- FAIL: TestAuditUpdateHasUpdateWithDroppedReadIndexes
```

No production code in this tree calls `Update.HasUpdate`, so the impact is limited to API consumers — reported as minor.

**Finding 1 boundary**

Added `TestAuditNodeUserReadIndexTwoTickTimeout`: with the same single-node cluster, a two-RTT timeout on the `INodeUser` path completes while the one-RTT timeout times out. That confirms the failure is exactly the one-tick dispatch delay, not a general read-path problem.

**Final state**

- Findings: F1 (`(*nodeUser).ReadIndex` misses the engine wakeup), F2 (`handleCandidateReadIndex` records a dropped ReadIndex twice), F3 (`pb.Update.HasUpdate` ignores dropped read indexes).
- Audit-tagged raft run: fuzz PASS, in-memory model PASS, vote-restart PASS, proposal control PASS; F2 (two tests) and F3 fail as documented. F1 fails under the audit tag in the root package.
- Default suites and `-race` (including the transport suite with generated TLS certs in the diagnostic copy) remain green; the implementation is byte-identical to `../source`.

[report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_20-19-30-dragonboat_raft-baseline/work/report.md) is reorganized as Summary → F1 → F2 → F3 → observations → reviewed areas → inventory → command log → unresolved work, and states that no executable coverage gap remains for buildable code.
